docs.title: Bonus Payload (Third-Party Media DOM Injection)
docs.text: Field Details Challenge ID CH-T1-05 Difficulty Tier ★☆☆☆☆☆ (1-Star) Category Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) / Content Spoofing OWASP Top 10 (2021) A03:2021 - Injection CWE ID CWE-79: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) CVSS v3.1 Base Score 4.3 (Medium) — CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N Target Technology Angular / Unrestricted Frame Embedding

docs.title: 1.1 Executive Overview
docs.text:
Beyond executing basic alert popups, Cross-Site Scripting vulnerabilities allow attackers to embed external third-party media, widgets, and dynamic interactive frames into the victim's session.

In this challenge, testing the search input DOM sink with an external media player iframe (SoundCloud widget with autoplay parameters) demonstrated that the application accepts arbitrary third-party content inclusion, exposing users to content spoofing, unsolicited audio/media playback, and tracking risks.

docs.title: 1.2 Business Impact Analysis
docs.text:
• Content Spoofing & Brand Damage: Malicious actors can embed offensive audio, video, or deceptive interfaces directly inside the official corporate domain.
  • Third-Party Tracking & Privacy Violations: Unauthorized iframes can set third-party tracking cookies or fingerprint visitors without consent under GDPR / ePrivacy directives.
  • Clickjacking Precursor: Demonstrates lack of frame-src restrictions in the security posture.

docs.title: 2.1 Inspection Workflow
docs.text:
1. Re-audited the unescaped search DOM sink identified in the DOM XSS assessment.
  2. Constructed a complex HTML injection payload embedding an external SoundCloud streaming player iframe: 
    <iframe width="100%" height="166" scrolling="no" frameborder="no" allow="autoplay" src="https://w.soundcloud.com/player/?url=https%3A//api.soundcloud.com/tracks/771984076&color=%23ff5500&auto_play=true&hide_related=false&show_comments=true&show_user=true&show_reposts=false&show_teaser=true"></iframe>
  3. Submitted the payload into the client search input.

docs.title: 3.1 Step-by-Step Reproduction
docs.text:
1. Open the search toolbar in OWASP Juice Shop (http://localhost:3000).
  2. Paste the SoundCloud iframe injection payload and execute search.
  3. The DOM sink renders the iframe element, initiating the external player stream within the page DOM.

Figure 1: External audio stream widget successfully injected and rendered in the application UI.

  1. The platform registers verification of the bonus payload injection.

Figure 2: Toast notification confirming completion of the Bonus Payload challenge.

docs.title: 4.1 Vulnerable Source Code
docs.text:
• Repository Location: frontend/src/app/search-result/search-result.component.ts
  • Root Cause Mechanism: The component passes raw search query inputs to bypassSecurityTrustHtml(), bypassing Angular's sanitization for both <script> tags and embedded <iframe> elements.

docs.title: 5.1 Content Security Policy (CSP) Frame Restrictions
docs.text:
To completely eliminate unauthorized external frame embedding regardless of DOM tampering:

Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; frame-src 'none'; object-src 'none';

If specific media providers are legitimately required, restrict to strict domain whitelists: 

Content-Security-Policy: frame-src 'self' https://w.soundcloud.com;

docs.title: Confidential Document Exposure
docs.text: Field Details Challenge ID CH-T1-03 Difficulty Tier ★☆☆☆☆☆ (1-Star) Category Broken Access Control / Sensitive Data Exposure OWASP Top 10 (2021) A01:2021 - Broken Access Control CWE ID CWE-552: Files or Directories Accessible to External Parties CVSS v3.1 Base Score 5.3 (Medium) — CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N Target Technology Express.js Static File Serving (serve-index)

docs.title: 1.1 Executive Overview
docs.text:
Web servers frequently store non-public operational assets, backups, or legacy files within storage directories. When public directory listing is enabled or file storage endpoints lack access control checks, external parties can browse directory structures and download proprietary business data.

In this assessment, the /ftp endpoint exposed a publicly accessible directory listing containing corporate documentation. An unauthenticated auditor was able to discover and download acquisitions.md, a confidential internal document outlining corporate mergers and acquisitions.

docs.title: 1.2 Business Impact Analysis
docs.text:
• Confidentiality: Direct disclosure of material non-public financial intelligence (mergers, intellectual property, corporate strategy).
  • Market & Legal Liability: Premature disclosure of acquisitions can trigger regulatory investigations (SEC / insider trading regulations) and breach confidentiality agreements (NDAs).
  • Reputational Harm: Loss of competitive advantage and erosion of partner trust.

docs.title: 2.1 Inspection Workflow
docs.text:
1. Performed directory enumeration on common static asset and legacy upload paths (/files, /uploads, /ftp, /public).
  2. Navigated to http://localhost:3000/ftp in the browser.
  3. Observed that the server utilizes the serve-index middleware, rendering an HTML index of files residing in the target folder.
  4. Identified sensitive files including acquisitions.md, eastere.gg, legal.md, and package.json.bak.

docs.text:

    actor Attacker as Security Auditor
    participant Web as Web Server (Express)
    participant FS as Local Filesystem (/ftp)

    Attacker->>Web: GET /ftp HTTP/1.1
    Web->>FS: Read directory index
    FS-->>Web: Return file listing
    Web-->>Attacker: Display directory table
    Attacker->>Web: GET /ftp/acquisitions.md
    Web->>FS: Fetch file stream
    FS-->>Web: File bytes
    Web-->>Attacker: 200 OK (Confidential Document Downloaded)

1. Open the web browser and browse to: 
    http://localhost:3000/ftp
  2. Inspect the rendered file list.

Figure 1: Publicly accessible directory indexing at /ftp exposing confidential documentation.

  1. Click on the hyperlink for acquisitions.md (or download directly via curl):

  2. The file contents are retrieved in plaintext, and the application triggers challenge resolution.

Figure 2: Toast notification confirming successful challenge verification.

docs.title: 4.1 Vulnerable Source Code
docs.text:
• Repository Location: server.ts
  • Vulnerable Code Pattern:
// INSECURE STATIC ASSET EXPOSURE
import serveIndex from 'serve-index';

// ⚠️ Flaw 1: Public directory indexing enabled on sensitive directory
app.use('/ftp', serveIndex('ftp', { icons: true }))

// ⚠️ Flaw 2: Static file delivery without authentication checks
app.use('/ftp', express.static('ftp'))

docs.title: 4.2 Root Cause Breakdown
docs.text:
• Insecure Default Middleware: Applying serve-index directly on an unauthenticated path exposes the entire directory inventory to untrusted visitors.
  • Absence of Least Privilege Isolation: Storing internal documentation inside the web root public directory instead of an isolated, encrypted document store.

docs.title: 5.1 Code Comparison (Before vs. After)
5.2 Defense-in-Depth Measures
docs.text:
1. Disable Directory Browsing: Ensure directory indexing modules are completely disabled in production web servers (e.g., Nginx autoindex off; or Apache Options -Indexes).
  2. Dedicated Cloud Storage: Store sensitive enterprise documents outside the web application container in an S3-compatible private bucket governed by IAM policies.

docs.text:
1. Re-request http://localhost:3000/ftp.
  2. Confirm the server returns 404 Not Found or 403 Forbidden.
  3. Verify that direct file paths (/ftp/acquisitions.md) cannot be retrieved without an authorized session.

docs.title: DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting (DOM XSS)
docs.text: Field Details Challenge ID CH-T1-04 Difficulty Tier ★☆☆☆☆☆ (1-Star) Category Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) / Injection OWASP Top 10 (2021) A03:2021 - Injection CWE ID CWE-79: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) CVSS v3.1 Base Score 6.1 (Medium) — CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N Target Technology Angular / Client-Side DOM Sink

docs.title: 1.1 Executive Overview
docs.text:
Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) occurs when untrusted user input is incorporated into an active web page without sufficient validation or output encoding. In a DOM-based XSS, the vulnerability resides purely on the client side: user-controlled data (the source) flows into an execution context in the browser DOM (the sink) without ever passing through or being sanitized by the backend server.

In this assessment, the product search field accepted HTML/JavaScript payloads and directly injected them into the Document Object Model using an iframe element, executing arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's session context.

docs.title: 1.2 Business Impact Analysis
docs.text:
• Session Hijacking: Attackers can extract authentication tokens (JWT in localStorage), session cookies, and sensitive user state.
  • Client-Side Account Takeover: Injected scripts can perform actions on behalf of the victim (placing unauthorized orders, changing passwords).
  • Phishing & Defacement: Injected iframes can overlay realistic credential harvest prompts over trusted application UI.

docs.title: 2.1 Inspection Workflow
docs.text:
1. Inspected the client-side search component in Angular (search-result.component.ts).
  2. Observed how the URL query parameter (?q=...) was reflected in the page UI: 
    http://localhost:3000/#/search?q=<test>
  3. Reviewed the component template and discovered the search string was rendered using Angular's bypassSecurityTrustHtml mechanism, explicitly disabling built-in Angular sanitization.

docs.title: 2.2 Attack Surface Sequence
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Attacker as Security Auditor
    participant Input as Search Input Field
    participant DOM as Browser DOM / Angular Sink
    participant Engine as JavaScript Engine

    Attacker->>Input: Submit <iframe src="javascript:alert(`xss`)">
    Input->>DOM: Value passed to bypassSecurityTrustHtml()
    DOM->>DOM: Inject raw iframe element into search header
    DOM->>Engine: Browser evaluates iframe src javascript uri
    Engine-->>Attacker: Execute alert('xss') dialog

docs.title: 3. Proof of Concept (PoC) & Exploitation
docs.text: [!NOTE] Testing executed on an isolated container target.

docs.title: 3.1 Step-by-Step Reproduction
docs.text:
1. Navigate to the main storefront at http://localhost:3000.
  2. Click the Search icon (magnifying glass) in the top-right toolbar.
  3. Input the standard iframe XSS vector: 
    <iframe src="javascript:alert(`xss`)">
  4. Press Enter.
  5. The browser evaluates the DOM injection, executing the script and displaying the JavaScript alert('xss') dialog.

Figure 1: Successful execution of client-side JavaScript via DOM-based XSS.

  1. Dismissing the dialog reveals the challenge completion notification.

Figure 2: OWASP Juice Shop confirmation notification for the DOM XSS challenge.

docs.title: 4.1 Vulnerable Source Code
docs.text:
• Repository Location: frontend/src/app/search-result/search-result.component.ts
  • Vulnerable Code Pattern:
// INSECURE DOM SANITIZATION BYPASS
import { DomSanitizer } from '@angular/platform-browser';

export class SearchResultComponent {
  constructor(private sanitizer: DomSanitizer) {}

  filterTable () {
    const query = this.route.snapshot.queryParams.q;
    // ⚠️ Flaw: Explicitly instructing Angular to bypass built-in HTML encoding
    this.searchValue = this.sanitizer.bypassSecurityTrustHtml(query);
  }
}

docs.title: 4.2 Root Cause Breakdown
docs.text: • Misuse of Security Bypass APIs: Angular by default sanitizes and escapes all interpolation expressions ({{ ... }}). The developer deliberately neutralized this protection by invoking DomSanitizer.bypassSecurityTrustHtml() on unsanitized user query parameters.

docs.title: 5.1 Code Comparison (Before vs. After)
5.2 Defense-in-Depth Measures
docs.text:
1. Content Security Policy (CSP): Deploy strict HTTP response headers disabling inline script evaluation and frame embedding: 
    Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; frame-src 'none';
  2. Static Analysis Rule (SAST): Configure ESLint rules (@angular-eslint/no-bypass-security-trust) in the CI/CD pipeline to block pull requests utilizing bypassSecurityTrust* methods without security team sign-off.

docs.title: 6.1 Retesting Procedure
docs.text:
1. Replace bypassSecurityTrustHtml with native text binding.
  2. Resubmit the payload <iframe src="javascript:alert(xss)"> in the search box.
  3. Confirm that the input is rendered as literal text (<iframe...>) without script execution or dialog popups.

docs.title: Error Handling Leak (Unhandled Exception)
docs.text: Field Details Challenge ID CH-T1-02 Difficulty Tier ★☆☆☆☆☆ (1-Star) Category Security Misconfiguration / Information Disclosure OWASP Top 10 (2021) A05:2021 - Security Misconfiguration CWE ID CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information CVSS v3.1 Base Score 5.3 (Medium) — CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N Target Technology Express.js / Node.js / Sequelize ORM / SQLite

docs.title: 1.1 Executive Overview
docs.text:
During standard web interaction, unexpected user inputs or malformed parameters can trigger edge-case exceptions within application logic. When an application lacks centralized error handling or runs in a debug configuration, the server may serialize raw internal error objects and stack traces directly into HTTP responses.

In this assessment, supplying an unhandled data type to a REST endpoint provoked an internal database exception. The application reflected a detailed Sequelize error stack trace revealing internal filesystem layouts, database technology versions, and raw SQL queries.

docs.title: 1.2 Business Impact Analysis
docs.text:
• Confidentiality: Exposure of internal server paths, runtime environments, package versions, and database schemas.
  • Attack Surface Expansion: Attackers utilize leaked stack traces to blueprint exact backend software versions and identify known CVEs or SQL injection vectors.
  • Compliance Deficiencies: Exposing internal system errors violates secure baseline requirements under standards such as PCI-DSS (Requirement 6.5.5) and OWASP ASVS v4.0.

docs.title: 2.1 Inspection Workflow
docs.text:
1. Intercepted and mapped REST API endpoints communicating between the Angular client and Express backend.
  2. Targeted the basket and product lookup endpoints which accept entity identifiers (e.g., /rest/basket/{id}).
  3. Injected boundary characters (single quote ', non-numeric characters, or special syntax) into numerical parameter slots: 
    GET /rest/basket/1' HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:3000
  4. Observed that the application returned an unhandled HTTP 500 Internal Server Error containing complete internal stack traces.

docs.title: 2.2 Attack Surface Sequence
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Tester as Security Auditor
    participant API as Express.js Router
    participant DB as Sequelize / SQLite

    Tester->>API: GET /rest/basket/1' (Malformed Input)
    API->>DB: Execute Query with raw parameter
    DB-->>API: Throw Unhandled Database Exception (SQL Syntax Error)
    API-->>Tester: HTTP 500 Response containing raw error.stack & file paths

docs.text: [!NOTE] Testing conducted on a local containerized target for defensive verification.

docs.title: 3.1 Step-by-Step Reproduction
docs.text:
1. Access the target application endpoint via browser or curl: 
    curl -i -s "http://localhost:3000/rest/basket/1'"
  2. Inspect the response body. The server returns a JSON error structure containing the SQLite dialect error and Node.js call stack.

Figure 1: Malformed input causing unhandled Sequelize error stack trace leakage.

  1. The application acknowledges resolution of the security challenge upon triggering the unhandled exception.

Figure 2: OWASP Juice Shop confirmation notification for the Error Handling challenge.

docs.title: 4.1 Vulnerable Source Code
docs.text:
• Repository Location: routes/basket.ts / Centralized error middleware
  • Vulnerable Code Pattern:
// VULNERABLE ROUTE HANDLER
export function basket () {
  return (req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction) => {
    const id = req.params.id
    BasketModel.findOne({ where: { id } })
      .then((basket: Basket | null) => {
        res.json(utils.queryResultToJson(basket))
      })
      .catch((error: Error) => {
        // ⚠️ Flaw: Passing raw error object directly to client response
        res.status(500).send(error)
      })
  }
}

docs.title: 4.2 Root Cause Breakdown
docs.text:
• Direct Error Serialization: In catch blocks, internal error objects (error or error.stack) are piped directly to res.send().
  • Missing Environment Guard: The application lacks a production environment toggle (NODE_ENV === 'production') to suppress verbose stack traces.

docs.title: 5.1 Code Comparison (Before vs. After)
5.2 Defense-in-Depth Measures
docs.text:
1. Global Error Middleware: Register a catch-all Express error-handling middleware ((err, req, res, next)) as the final handler in the pipeline.
  2. Input Validation: Enforce strict type constraints (e.g. validating that :id is strictly an integer) using validators such as express-validator or zod prior to database queries.

docs.title: 6.1 Retesting Procedure
docs.text:
1. Send a malformed payload to the endpoint (/rest/basket/invalid').
  2. Verify that the response returns a generic message (An unexpected error occurred) and HTTP 400/500 without stack or internal path strings.

docs.title: Exposed Metrics (Prometheus Infrastructure Leak)
docs.text: Field Details Challenge ID CH-T1-10 Difficulty Tier ★☆☆☆☆☆ (1-Star) Category Security Misconfiguration / Information Disclosure OWASP Top 10 (2021) A05:2021 - Security Misconfiguration CWE ID CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor CVSS v3.1 Base Score 5.3 (Medium) — CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N Target Technology Prometheus Metrics / Express epimetheus Middleware

docs.title: 1.1 Executive Overview
docs.text:
Modern cloud-native and microservice architectures export operational runtime metrics to collectors such as Prometheus or Datadog. These telemetry feeds provide detailed instrumentation on CPU utilization, memory pressure, active database connection pools, garbage collection timings, and exact HTTP request rates per endpoint.

A critical security misconfiguration arises when monitoring scrapers (/metrics or /actuator/prometheus) are bound to the public-facing application router rather than an isolated administrative port or internal VPC interface.

docs.title: 1.2 Business Impact Analysis
docs.text:
• Reconnaissance & Architecture Disclosure: Attackers obtain real-time metrics on server load, system bottlenecks, and internal API usage patterns.
  • Timing & DoS Amplification: Real-time metrics allow adversaries to accurately measure the efficacy of denial-of-service (DoS) or resource exhaustion attacks.
  • Compliance Exposure: Violates network segregation and least-privilege observability principles (NIST CSF PR.AC-5).

docs.title: 2.1 Inspection Workflow
docs.text:
1. Performed an endpoint wordlist enumeration covering common DevOps and telemetry paths (/metrics, /health, /actuator, /debug, /status).
  2. Sent a GET request to http://localhost:3000/metrics.
  3. Observed that the server responded with HTTP 200 containing raw Prometheus telemetry formatted in plaintext key-value pairs without requiring authentication.

docs.title: 3.1 Step-by-Step Reproduction
docs.text:
1. Open a browser or terminal and request the monitoring path: 
    curl -i http://localhost:3000/metrics

Figure 1: Publicly accessible Prometheus metrics exposing internal Node.js telemetry.

  1. The application logs the access and awards challenge verification.

Figure 2: Toast notification confirming completion of the Exposed Metrics challenge.

• Repository Location: server.ts

// PUBLIC METRICS EXPOSURE
import epimetheus from 'epimetheus';

// ⚠️ Flaw: Metrics collection endpoint attached to public router with zero authentication
epimetheus.instrument(app)

docs.title: 4.2 Root Cause Breakdown
docs.text: • Public Port Binding: The epimetheus middleware was registered on the primary application instance, automatically creating the /metrics endpoint accessible over the public internet port 3000.

docs.title: Outdated Whitelist (Open Redirect via Legacy Address)
docs.text: Field Details Challenge ID CH-T1-09 Difficulty Tier ★☆☆☆☆☆ (1-Star) Category Unvalidated Redirects and Forwards / Broken Access Control OWASP Top 10 (2021) A01:2021 - Broken Access Control CWE ID CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect') CVSS v3.1 Base Score 4.7 (Medium) — CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:N/I:L/A:N Target Technology Express.js Redirection Middleware

docs.title: 1.1 Executive Overview
docs.text:
Web applications often utilize redirection endpoints (e.g. /redirect?to=...) to route users to external payment gateways, documentation, or social platforms. To prevent Open Redirect attacks (where attackers lure victims to phishing domains under the guise of a trusted company URL), developers implement domain whitelists.

A common lifecycle flaw occurs when whitelists are not regularly audited: legacy external domains, expired vendor services, or deprecated cryptocurrency donation addresses remain whitelisted long after the organization ceases using them.

docs.title: 1.2 Business Impact Analysis
docs.text:
• Phishing Credibility Amplification: Attackers construct phishing campaigns using the trusted primary domain (https://trusted-site.com/redirect?to=https://attacker-domain.com).
  • Reputational Degradation: Association with abandoned third-party services or domain takeovers.

docs.title: 2.1 Inspection Workflow
docs.text:
1. Located the redirect controller in the server code (routes/redirect.ts).
  2. Inspected the URL parameter verification logic: 
    export function performRedirect () {
  return (req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction) => {
    const toUrl = req.query.to
    if (security.isAuthorizedUrl(toUrl)) {
      res.redirect(toUrl)
    } else {
      res.status(406).send('Unrecognized target URL')
    }
  }
}
  3. Audited the whitelist array inside lib/utils.ts and discovered an unmaintained legacy Bitcoin address on blockchain.info.

docs.title: 3.1 Step-by-Step Reproduction
docs.text:
1. Dispatch an HTTP GET request to the redirect endpoint targeting the legacy whitelist entry: 
    http://localhost:3000/redirect?to=https://blockchain.info/address/1AbKfgHTnnJhmGCJk8R3mA7xNyHbgegCDT

Figure 1: Executing redirection to the legacy cryptocurrency donation address.

  1. The application validates the target against its outdated whitelist and issues an HTTP 302 redirect.
  2. Returning to the Score Board confirms the challenge has been completed.

Figure 2: Toast notification confirming resolution of the Outdated Whitelist challenge.

• Repository Location: lib/utils.ts

// STALE WHITELIST CONFIGURATION
export const redirectWhitelist = [
  'https://github.com/bkimminich/juice-shop',
  // ⚠️ Flaw: Abandoned third-party cryptocurrency address remains trusted
  'https://blockchain.info/address/1AbKfgHTnnJhmGCJk8R3mA7xNyHbgegCDT',
  'https://gratipay.com/juice-shop'
]

docs.title: 4.2 Root Cause Breakdown
docs.text: • Stale Whitelist Hygiene: Inadequate lifecycle auditing of authorized external domains allowed deprecated URLs to retain trusted status within security routing middleware.

docs.title: 1.1 Executive Overview
docs.text:
During the reconnaissance phase of a web application security assessment, auditors analyze public disclosures, legal statements, and privacy policies. Privacy policies frequently enumerate internal data handling practices, third-party analytics vendors, data retention schedules, and cross-border data transfer protocols.

In this introductory challenge, the privacy policy route (/#/privacy-security/privacy-policy) is navigated to verify compliance with privacy disclosure mandates and inspect declared security controls.

  • Third-Party Risk Assessment: Identifying declared third-party sub-processors assists security auditors in mapping external data flows.

docs.title: Repetitive Registration (Client-Side Only Validation Bypass)
docs.text: Field Details Challenge ID CH-T1-06 Difficulty Tier ★☆☆☆☆☆ (1-Star) Category Improper Input Validation / Insecure Design OWASP Top 10 (2021) A04:2021 - Insecure Design CWE ID CWE-602: Client-Side Enforcement of Server-Side Security CVSS v3.1 Base Score 4.3 (Medium) — CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N Target Technology Angular Reactive Forms vs Express User Route

docs.title: 1.1 Executive Overview
docs.text:
Modern web applications frequently validate form inputs on the client side using frontend framework validators to provide responsive UX feedback (e.g. confirming that "Repeat Password" matches "Password"). A critical security vulnerability arises when development teams treat client-side validation as a security boundary and fail to enforce identical validation rules at the backend API layer.

In this assessment, the user registration page enforces password matching solely within the Angular client UI. An attacker can manipulate DOM properties or submit direct API payloads where the repeated password does not match, which the server processes without verification.

docs.title: 1.2 Business Impact Analysis
docs.text:
• Data Integrity: Allows corrupted, malformed, or automated rogue user accounts to be provisioned.
  • Account Recovery Lockout: If a user mistypes their initial password while bypassing confirmation, they may lock themselves out of newly created accounts.
  • Violations of Secure Coding Baselines: Demonstrates absence of unified input validation architectures across client and server boundaries.

docs.title: 2.1 Inspection Workflow
docs.text:
1. Inspected the registration form at http://localhost:3000/#/register.
  2. Reviewed the network traffic when the registration form is submitted. The client makes a JSON POST request to /api/Users.
  3. Observed the payload body: 
    {
  "email": "user@target.com",
  "password": "Password123!",
  "passwordRepeat": "Password123!",
  "securityQuestion": { ... },
  "securityAnswer": "..."
}
  4. Discovered that the backend User model schema only indexes email and password, ignoring passwordRepeat entirely.

docs.title: 2.2 Attack Surface Sequence
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Attacker as Security Auditor
    participant DOM as Browser Form / DevTools
    participant API as Express API (/api/Users)
    participant DB as SQLite Users Table

    Attacker->>DOM: Enter Password != Repeat Password
    Attacker->>DOM: Remove disabled attribute on Register Button via Console
    Attacker->>DOM: Click Register Button
    DOM->>API: POST /api/Users (Mismatched Passwords)
    API->>API: Evaluate schema (No server-side equality check!)
    API->>DB: INSERT INTO Users (email, password)
    DB-->>API: User Created
    API-->>Attacker: HTTP 201 Created (Challenge Solved)

docs.title: 3.1 Step-by-Step Reproduction
docs.text:
1. Navigate to http://localhost:3000/#/register.
  2. Fill in the email, password, and security question.
  3. Open Developer Tools Console (F12) and supply mismatched password parameters while clearing the submit button's disabled state: 
    document.getElementById('repeatPasswordControl').value = 'CompletelyDifferentPassword';
document.getElementById('registerButton').removeAttribute('disabled');
document.getElementById('registerButton').click();

Figure 1: Client-side registration form successfully submitted with non-matching password confirmation.

  1. The server accepts the registration, creating the user and completing the challenge.

Figure 2: Toast notification confirming resolution of the Repetitive Registration challenge.

docs.title: 4.1 Vulnerable Source Code
docs.text:
• Repository Location: routes/register.ts
  • Vulnerable Code Pattern:
// INSECURE BACKEND REGISTRATION HANDLER
export function register () {
  return (req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction) => {
    // ⚠️ Flaw: Backend takes req.body directly without validating equality of password and passwordRepeat
    UserModel.create({
      email: req.body.email,
      password: req.body.password,
      role: roles.customer
    })
    .then((user: User) => {
      res.status(201).json({ status: 'success', data: user })
    })
    .catch((error: Error) => {
      next(error)
    })
  }
}

docs.title: 4.2 Root Cause Breakdown
docs.text: • Client-Side Reliance: The backend completely trusts incoming HTTP parameters, assuming that because the Angular UI checked password === passwordRepeat, no mismatched request could ever reach the server.

docs.title: Finding the Hidden Score Board
docs.text: Field Details Challenge ID CH-T1-01 Difficulty Tier ★☆☆☆☆☆ (1-Star) Category Security Misconfiguration / Information Disclosure OWASP Top 10 (2021) A05:2021 - Security Misconfiguration CWE ID CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor CVSS v3.1 Base Score 3.1 (Low) — CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N Target Technology Angular (SPA) / TypeScript Routing

docs.title: 1.1 Executive Overview
docs.text:
Modern Single Page Applications (SPAs) built with frameworks like Angular or React compile routing rules into client-side JavaScript bundles. In this application, developers intentionally hid the Score Board challenge tracker from standard navigation menus, assuming that omitting visible UI links would prevent unauthorized or public access.

This anti-pattern is known as Security through Obscurity. Because the entire routing table is delivered directly to the end-user's browser, unauthenticated visitors can reverse-engineer internal paths and access administrative or unlisted functionality directly.

docs.title: 1.2 Business Impact Analysis
docs.text:
• Confidentiality: Exposure of internal operational dashboards, system tracking metrics, or unreleased feature interfaces to untrusted parties.
  • Integrity: Potential reconnaissance leverage for attackers to discover high-value endpoints or debug interfaces.
  • Compliance & Governance: Failure to enforce strict role-based access control (RBAC) at both client and server boundaries violates principle-of-least-privilege guidelines (NIST SP 800-53, ISO 27001).

docs.title: 2.1 Inspection Workflow
docs.text:
1. Opened the target web application at http://localhost:3000 using Google Chrome Developer Tools (F12).
  2. Navigated to the Sources tab to analyze loaded client-side bundles under localhost:3000.
  3. Located the primary compiled application bundle (main.js).
  4. Reformatted the minified JavaScript using the Pretty-print ({}) utility to facilitate source inspection.
  5. Executed a targeted string query (Ctrl + F) searching for route declarations matching score-board and path:.
  6. Discovered the unauthenticated client-side route definition: 
    { path: "score-board", component: ScoreBoardComponent }

docs.title: 2.2 Attack Surface Sequence
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Attacker as Security Tester
    participant Browser as Browser (DevTools)
    participant Client as Angular Client Router
    participant View as Score Board View

    Attacker->>Browser: Inspect main.js bundle
    Browser-->>Attacker: Disclose route definition 'score-board'
    Attacker->>Client: Navigate to http://target/#/score-board
    Client->>Client: Evaluate route table (No Guard present)
    Client-->>View: Render Score Board interface
    View-->>Attacker: Full access to challenge tracker

docs.title: 3. Proof of Concept (PoC) & Exploitation
docs.text: [!NOTE] Testing was performed in a local, isolated Docker container environment for defensive audit purposes.

docs.title: 3.1 Step-by-Step Reproduction
docs.text:
1. Launch the application in the web browser at http://localhost:3000.
  2. Inspect main.js in DevTools to confirm the route naming convention.

Figure 1: Client-side source code audit in Developer Tools revealing the unlisted score-board route.

  1. Manually append /#/score-board to the browser address bar: 
    GET /#/score-board HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:3000
  2. The Angular client immediately resolves the route and instantiates the ScoreBoardComponent.
  3. The application confirms verification of the vulnerability with a success notification banner.

Figure 2: Accessing the Score Board interface and receiving the challenge resolution notification.

docs.title: 4.1 Vulnerable Source Code
docs.text:
• Repository File: frontend/src/app/app.routing.ts
  • Component: ScoreBoardComponent
// VULNERABLE ROUTE CONFIGURATION
const routes: Routes = [
  {
    path: 'score-board',
    component: ScoreBoardComponent
    // ⚠️ Flaw: No route guard (canActivate) is attached to enforce authentication or role verification
  },
  // ... other routes
]

docs.title: 4.2 Root Cause Breakdown
docs.text:
• Client-Side Absence of Guards: The Angular router configuration defines score-board as a public top-level route without implementing an Angular CanActivate guard interface.
  • Architectural Misconception: Reliance on UI menu omission rather than cryptographic or state-based access verification to restrict sensitive views.

docs.title: 5.1 Code Comparison (Before vs. After)
5.2 Defense-in-Depth Measures
docs.text:
1. Server-Side API Authorization: Frontend route guards provide user experience protection, but the backend API endpoint serving scorecard data (/api/Challenges) must independently validate the user's JWT token and permissions on every request.
  2. Bundle Hardening: In production applications, administrative routes and components should be encapsulated in lazily-loaded feature modules (loadChildren) accessible only after successful authentication, reducing the footprint of the public main.js bundle.

docs.title: 6.1 Retesting Procedure
docs.text:
1. Apply the canActivate: [AuthGuard] guard to the route configuration.
  2. Attempt direct navigation to http://localhost:3000/#/score-board in an unauthenticated browser session.
  3. Confirm that the application redirects the user to /#/login with an access-denied flash message.

docs.title: Zero Stars Feedback (Business Logic & Boundary Bypass)
docs.text: Field Details Challenge ID CH-T1-07 Difficulty Tier ★☆☆☆☆☆ (1-Star) Category Improper Input Validation / Business Logic Flaw OWASP Top 10 (2021) A04:2021 - Insecure Design CWE ID CWE-20: Improper Input Validation CVSS v3.1 Base Score 4.3 (Medium) — CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N Target Technology Angular Slider Component / Express Feedback API

docs.title: 1.1 Executive Overview
docs.text:
E-commerce and review platforms rely on strict rating rating boundaries (typically 1 to 5 stars) to calculate accurate product quality indices, merchant trust metrics, and recommendation algorithms. When boundary constraints are applied solely via user interface controls (such as Angular Material sliders) without backend mathematical enforcement, users can bypass limits through direct API manipulation.

In this assessment, the customer feedback mechanism prevented users from selecting fewer than 1 star within the graphical interface. However, transmitting a rating value of 0 directly via an intercepted API request was accepted and stored by the database.

docs.title: 1.2 Business Impact Analysis
docs.text:
• Data Integrity Corruption: Submitting out-of-bounds ratings skews algorithmic averages, reviews, and automated recommendation engines.
  • Potential Negative Rating Denial of Service: In poorly implemented average calculations, unexpected values (0 or negative integers) can lead to division-by-zero errors or broken analytics pipelines.

docs.title: 2.1 Inspection Workflow
docs.text:
1. Navigated to the Customer Feedback page (/#/contact).
  2. Observed the rating widget implemented using an Angular Material <mat-slider> component configured with min="1" and max="5".
  3. Intercepted the form submission request in Burp Suite / Browser Network tab: 
    POST /api/Feedbacks HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:3000
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "comment": "Sample feedback",
  "rating": 1
}
  4. Hypothesized that the backend does not validate minimum integer boundaries.

docs.title: 3.1 Step-by-Step Reproduction
docs.text:
1. Open the Customer Feedback page at http://localhost:3000/#/contact.
  2. Enter a feedback comment and solve the visual CAPTCHA.
  3. Open Developer Tools Console (F12) and dispatch an unconstrained API request: 
    fetch('/api/Feedbacks', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ comment: "Devastating review", rating: 0 })
}).then(r => r.json()).then(data => console.log("Response:", data));

Figure 1: Executing an out-of-bounds rating payload of 0 stars via client console.

  1. The API responds with 201 Created, storing the zero-star review and solving the challenge.

Figure 2: Toast notification confirming the Zero Stars feedback submission.

docs.title: 4.1 Vulnerable Source Code
docs.text:
• Repository Location: data/static/models/feedback.ts
  • Vulnerable Code Pattern:
// INSECURE DATABASE SCHEMA DEFINITION
Feedback.init({
  comment: {
    type: DataTypes.STRING,
    allowNull: false
  },
  rating: {
    type: DataTypes.INTEGER,
    allowNull: false
    // ⚠️ Flaw: Missing Sequelize validation bounds (min: 1, max: 5)
  }
}, { sequelize, modelName: 'Feedback' })

docs.title: 4.2 Root Cause Breakdown
docs.text: • Missing ORM Model Constraints: The database column definition accepts any valid integer without specifying Sequelize validation constraints (validate: { min: 1, max: 5 }).

docs.title: Login Admin (SQL Injection Authentication Bypass)
docs.text: Field Details Challenge ID CH-T2-01 Difficulty Tier ★★☆☆☆☆ (2-Star) Category Injection OWASP Top 10 (2021) A03:2021 - Injection CWE ID CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection') CVSS v3.1 Base Score 9.8 (Critical) — CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H Target Technology Node.js / Express / Sequelize ORM / SQLite

docs.title: 1.1 Executive Overview
docs.text:
SQL Injection (SQLi) is one of the most critical vulnerabilities affecting data-driven web applications. It occurs when untrusted client input is directly concatenated into a dynamic SQL query without parameterization or proper sanitization.

In this assessment, the authentication endpoint /rest/user/login accepted user-supplied email strings directly into a dynamic database lookup. By supplying a single quote (') followed by boolean logic and SQL comment delimiters, an unauthenticated attacker bypassed the password verification check entirely and obtained administrative session privileges.

docs.title: 1.2 Business Impact Analysis
docs.text:
• Total Compromise of Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability: Administrative access grants full read/write/delete privileges over the customer database, product inventory, and financial transaction records.
  • Regulatory Non-Compliance: Unprotected SQL execution leading to PII breach violates GDPR Article 32 and PCI-DSS Requirement 6.5.1.
  • Identity Theft & Account Takeover: Attackers can masquerade as system operators and manipulate underlying infrastructure settings.

docs.title: 2.1 Inspection & Fuzzing Workflow
docs.text:
1. Intercepted the login request using Burp Suite Proxy: 
    POST /rest/user/login HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:3000
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "email": "tester@test.com",
  "password": "Password123"
}
  2. Sent the request to Burp Suite Repeater (Ctrl + R) for boundary testing.
  3. Fuzzed the email field by injecting a single quote character (').
  4. The server returned an unhandled HTTP 500 error exposing a raw database exception: 
    {
  "error": "SQLITE_ERROR: unrecognized token: \"' AND password = '...'\""
}
  5. This confirmed that the parameter is directly interpolated into raw SQL queries without parameter binding.

docs.title: 2.2 Attack Surface Sequence
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram

    actor Attacker as Security Auditor

docs.title: 3. Proof of Concept (PoC) & Exploitation
docs.text: [!NOTE] Performed on an isolated Docker lab instance for ethical security testing.

docs.title: 3.1 Step-by-Step Reproduction
docs.text:
1. Send the following crafted request via Burp Suite Repeater or the web login form:
  2. Email: ' OR 1=1 --
  3. Password: any_dummy_password
  4. The query executes as WHERE email = '' OR 1=1, returning the first row in the Users table which corresponds to admin@juice-sh.op.
  5. The server signs and returns an administrative JSON Web Token (JWT).

Figure 1: Successful SQL Injection authentication bypass executed in Burp Suite Repeater.

  1. Authenticating with the token in the browser confirms administrative rights and triggers the challenge completion toast.

Figure 2: Toast notification confirming successful authentication as the application administrator.

docs.title: 4.1 Vulnerable Source Code
docs.text:
• Repository Location: routes/login.ts
  • Vulnerable Code Pattern:
// INSECURE AUTHENTICATION QUERY CONCATENATION
models.sequelize.query(
  `SELECT * FROM Users WHERE email = '${req.body.email || ''}' AND password = '${security.hash(req.body.password || '')}' AND deletedAt IS NULL`,
  { model: models.User, plain: true }
)
.then((authenticatedUser: { data: User }) => {
  const user = utils.queryResultToJson(authenticatedUser)
  const token = security.authorize(user)
  res.json({ authentication: { token, user } })
})
.catch((error: Error) => {
  next(error)
})

docs.title: 4.2 Root Cause Breakdown
docs.text:
• String Interpolation: The code uses ES6 template literals (`${req.body.email}`) to construct the SQL query directly instead of passing parameters through the ORM abstraction layer.
  • Premature Password Hashing: Even though security.hash() is called on the password, commenting out the remainder of the query with -- renders password validation completely inert.

docs.title: 5.1 Code Comparison (Before vs. After)
5.2 Defense-in-Depth Measures
docs.text:
1. Parameterized Queries (Prepared Statements): Parameter binding ensures input data is treated strictly as literal values rather than executable SQL syntax.
  2. Account Lockout & Rate Limiting: Apply rate limiters (express-rate-limit) to prevent rapid authentication tampering and fuzzing.
  3. Web Application Firewall (WAF): Enforce signature and anomaly detection for SQL metacharacters (' OR 1=1) at the gateway layer.

docs.title: Secure Coding Guidelines: Node.js, Express & Angular
docs.text: This guide consolidates defensive engineering principles and remediation patterns identified across the OWASP Juice Shop application security assessment.

docs.title: 1.1 SQL & NoSQL Injection Defense
docs.text:
• Sequelize ORM Parameterization: Never concatenate untrusted strings into raw SQL queries. 
    // ❌ VULNERABLE
sequelize.query(`SELECT * FROM Products WHERE id = ${req.params.id}`);

// ✅ SECURE
sequelize.query('SELECT * FROM Products WHERE id = :id', {
  replacements: { id: req.params.id },
  type: QueryTypes.SELECT
});
  • NoSQL Query Sanitization: Use mongo-sanitize to strip $ and . operators from request bodies to prevent operator injection ({"$gt": ""}).

docs.title: 1.2 Access Control & Authorization (IDOR Defense)
docs.text:
• Always validate that the authenticated user (req.user.id) owns the requested object before fetching or mutating records. 
    // ❌ VULNERABLE (IDOR)
const basket = await BasketModel.findByPk(req.params.basketId);

// ✅ SECURE
const basket = await BasketModel.findOne({
  where: {
    id: req.params.basketId,
    UserId: req.user.id
  }
});
if (!basket) return res.status(404).json({ error: "Basket not found" });

docs.title: 1.3 Security Headers & Middleware
docs.text:
• Integrate Helmet.js to automatically set modern HTTP defense headers: 
    const helmet = require('helmet');
app.use(helmet({
  contentSecurityPolicy: {
    directives: {
      defaultSrc: ["'self'"],
      scriptSrc: ["'self'"],
      objectSrc: ["'none'"]
    }
  },
  frameguard: { action: 'deny' },
  hsts: { maxAge: 31536000, includeSubDomains: true }
}));

docs.title: 2.1 Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Prevention
docs.text:
• Rely on Angular's built-in contextual encoding:
  • Use {{ expression }} or [property]="value" bindings.
  • Avoid DomSanitizer.bypassSecurityTrustHtml() unless strictly validated and sanitized with DOMPurify.
  • Never use native ElementRef.nativeElement.innerHTML = ....

docs.title: 2.2 Client-Side Route Guards & Authentication
docs.text: • Frontend route guards (canActivate) are for user experience only. All business logic and data access must be authoritatively enforced on the backend API server.
